name: Puente romano de Mérida

position.source: https://www.openstreetmap.org/way/1075066789 (the middle of the footway on the bridge, ways 25024396 + 1075066789 + 391413815, 783.7 m; heading = the downstream face, 90° from the axis between the two ends, 51.45°)

rights.note: Roman bridge of Augusta Emerita, built with the founding of the colony (late 1st century BC); repaired in 483, the middle stretch rebuilt in 1603–1611 and repaired again after 1812, 1823 and 1860. Builders unknown. Bien de Interés Cultural (1912) and part of the UNESCO World Heritage site «Archaeological Ensemble of Mérida» (1993).

notes: Built by code (model_sources/Q588535_puente_romano_de_merida.py, tools/meshkit.py) with AI assistance. 60 semicircular granite arches built procedurally along the OSM axis (it bends only about 0.3°, at San Antonio): 31 piers where OSM has them (two long gaps split in two) and 29 evenly spaced arches over the south-western bank, where OSM has none. The Roman stretches have semicircular cutwaters upstream up to the springing; the middle one (Humilladero to San Antonio) sharp cutwaters with pyramidal caps and buttresses downstream; relief arches over the piers except over the dry bank; voussoirs, cornice band, parapets with coping, the two round balconies at x = −157 and the two descendederos (Humilladero down to the island, San Antonio with its pointed end). y = 0 is the water (202.0 m, MDT05); deck from 8.8 m at the city end to 12 m over the river and 5.3 m at the far end. Uncertain: the spacing and size of the arches of the south-western stretch (no piers in OSM: 10.7 m bays taken), the height profile of the deck (±1 m), the exact sizes of the piers (4.2/5.0/4.0/3.6 m by stretch), the footings, the descendederos' slopes. Street lamps left out. ground: keep with ground_fit false (a bridge over water).
